I wish to express my deep concern over recent developments involving my relationship with the Governor of Kano State, His Excellency Abba Kabir Yusuf, and the alleged use of anti-corruption institutions for political purposes.

His Excellency Abba Kabir Yusuf once served under me in various capacities, including as my Personal Assistant (PA), Principal Private Secretary (PPS), and Commissioner. He was also our movement’s anointed candidate in both the 2019 and 2023 general elections, emerging victorious in 2023 through our collective efforts. 

The longstanding relationship of 43 years with him and trust I reposed in him afforded him access to information and insight into the value I place on personal integrity, trust that has, regrettably, been misused and abused. 

It is on this basis that I believe he is determined to drag me and my family into public controversy by leveraging reputable government agencies, particularly the EFCC, in an attempt to tarnish the public image I have spent nearly fifty years building.

We believe that some months ago the Governor personally submitted a formal request to the EFCC seeking to come after me. After failing to compel the Commission, owing to its institutional integrity and established procedures, he resorted to a little-known body called the Society for Anti-Corruption and Good Governance Initiative (SACGGI). This organisation is neither registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) nor does it possess any verifiable digital presence or formal relationship with the EFCC or ICPC. 

It was used to stage physical protests at the EFCC premises in a deliberate attempt to exert pressure on the agency. We further believe that the Governor and certain members of his cabinet continue to deploy the media to advance this campaign against my reputation.

Information is being selectively leaked and amplified through the media and other public platforms to portray the situation in the worst possible light. 

Coming as it does within the context of the electioneering season, these actions appear calculated to distract attention from substantive issues, undermine our credibility, and weaken our capacity to contest and win elections in 2027. Such efforts are also heating the polity and making the peace and security of Kano State more fragile. 

The campaign is not limited to me and my candidature; it extends to other candidates, particularly the Kano State gubernatorial candidate, Comrade Aminu Abdussalam who is currently defending his ticket before INEC and the courts. This constitutes a further attempt by the Governor to manipulate elements within reputable institutions, INEC and the judiciary to prevent the publication of our candidate’s name and ultimately bar him from contesting the 2027 general election, so that the Governor may run unopposed.

I wish to thank the EFCC for the professional manner in which it has handled the two previous invitations extended to me during my years in public service, and for the prudence it has demonstrated throughout.

I thank God that more than eleven years after leaving the Kano State Government, having served two full terms as Governor spanning eight years, in addition to seventeen years in the civil service, service as Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives during the aborted Third Republic, as an elected delegate to the 1994–1995 Constitutional Conference, as Minister of Defence, as Special Adviser to the President on Darfur, as a member representing the Northwest on the Niger Delta Development Commission, and as a member of the 8th Senate, I have maintained a clean record. 

On this note, I advise younger and serving public office holders to tread with caution. Public office is transient; those who live in glass houses should be careful about throwing stones.

I also appreciate members of the general public who have refused to be misled by these efforts, and especially those who have spoken in defence of our reputation and record.

Premier League Statement

Sanctions imposed on Manchester City

Following the dismissal of Manchester City FC’s appeal, an independent Commission has determined the sanctions for the Club’s breaches of the Premier League Rules.

The independent Commission previously found Manchester City FC guilty of 114 of the 115 charges relating to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, and of the majority of the charges relating to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation. The Appeal Board has upheld those findings.

The Commission has concluded that the Club arranged “sham” contracts and related agreements as part of a disguised funding scheme. These arrangements artificially inflated the Club’s revenues and reduced its costs by more than £900 million, resulting in the filing of misstated accounts and the concealment of its true financial position from auditors and football regulators. The Club was also found to have made concerted efforts to frustrate the Premier League’s investigation.

The sanctions imposed are as follows:

1. Expulsion and relegation
   Manchester City FC is expelled from membership of the Premier League. Expulsion and relegation will take effect on 1st June 2027. From that date, the Club will no longer be a member of the Premier League and will be required to participate in the EFL Championship from the 2027/28 season, subject to any applicable EFL processes.

2. Stripping of domestic titles
   All domestic titles won by Manchester City FC during and after the period of the established breaches are declared null and void and are stripped from the Club. These are:  
   - Premier League titles: 2011/12, 2013/14, 2017/18, 2018/19, 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24  
   - FA Cups: 2010/11, 2018/19 and 2022/23  
   - EFL Cup / League Cup titles: 2013/14, 2015/16, 2017/18, 2018/19, 2019/20 and 2020/21  
   - Related Community Shields  

   The titles are vacated. Where appropriate, the runners-up in the relevant competitions will be recognised as the winners. Prize money, medals and other associated benefits will be adjusted accordingly. The FA has confirmed corresponding action in respect of the FA Cup and Community Shield.

3. Financial penalty
   A fine of £250 million is imposed, payable according to a schedule set by the Commission. This is in addition to any costs orders arising from the proceedings.

4. Transfer and registration restrictions
   A three-window transfer ban (incoming and outgoing, with limited exceptions for expiring contracts or mutual terminations) and a corresponding registration embargo are imposed, effective from the next available transfer window after 1 June 2027.

5. Points deduction
   A deduction of 70 points is applied with immediate effect to any remaining fixtures of the 2026/27 season in which the Club participates prior to the effective date of relegation.

6. Further requirements
   The Club is required to submit to enhanced independent financial monitoring, oversight of commercial contracts, and full co-operation with regulatory requirements for a minimum period of five seasons. Fitness-and-propriety reviews may be undertaken in respect of relevant individuals connected to the breaches.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, said:  
“These sanctions reflect the scale, duration and deliberate nature of the breaches. The independent process has established that the rules agreed by the clubs were systematically circumvented. Protecting the integrity and fairness of the competition remains the League’s primary responsibility.”

Manchester City FC has the right to appeal the sanction decision. Any appeal will be heard by a further independent Appeal Board. Unless a stay is granted, the sanctions take effect as set out above, with expulsion and relegation effective from 1 June 2027.

The full reasoned decisions will be published in due course, subject to necessary redactions.

🚨🇺🇸🇮🇷 U.S. F-35s over the Middle East are reportedly flying with never-before-seen white Sidewinder missiles... and the Air Force won't say why

Air Force photos since early November show F-35As in the region carrying the heat-seeking missiles painted almost entirely white or light gray, a scheme spotted nowhere else in the world.

The standard version has a dark nose and dark fins.

The leading theory is a version the Navy built just for the F-35 with special coatings to keep the jet harder to spot on radar, since the stealth fighter has to carry these missiles outside, under its wings.

Those missiles have existed for years, yet they're only showing up now, over Iran's doorstep.

And by putting the photos out in the middle of this war, the Air Force clearly wants Tehran to notice.

Source: The War Zone / Writer: Daniel https://t.co/fiICLL5Q0w

🚨 BREAKING: Colorado DNA analyst Yvonne “Missy” Woods sentenced to 10 years after deleting male DNA in 32 rape cases — then reporting none was found.

She spent 29 years as CBI’s star expert. Investigators now say 1,045 of her cases are tainted. Over 400 were sexual assaults. One murder conviction already tossed.

An intern caught her. Concerns were raised more than a decade earlier. She kept testing rape kits anyway.
In court, supporters packed the room. Victims shouted “LIAR! LIAR! LIAR!” as she was cuffed and led out.

Colorado is now retesting more than 1,000 cases. 

Prosecutors already cut plea deals in three murder cases rather than risk her work in front of a jury.
